decision: Which hero should open the page? (Everything below the hero is the same in all three.)
invariants: same copy (D-024 hero, D-017 page story)
same tokens: white, hairline grid, sun/sky/tang/leaf tiles, Zodiak + Switzer

options.bet: Primer-style: a row of real-looking kids holding their workbooks, then the claim in a ruled box with colour tiles
options.benefit: Strongest brand moment; looks like a confident company
options.cost: The product loop is not visible until you scroll
options.risk: The lineup is AI-generated; parents may sense it, and it shows kids, not the product

options.bet: Outschool/Squirrel-style: the claim on the left, the six-step loop as connected photos and chips on the right
options.benefit: Explains how it works in the first screen (the 15-second test)
options.cost: Busier; six small images compete with the headline
options.risk: On phones the loop becomes a 2x3 grid and loses the path

options.bet: Ello-style: centred claim over one big photo of a child at home, with a marked page and a live progress report floating on it
options.benefit: Warmest; shows the product result (marked page + report) in one look
options.cost: Relies on one photo carrying the brand
options.risk: Stock photo; the report card may read as an app, not paper
